title: Road Quest
appreciation: That is how a responsible road user thinks.
corrections: Something important was easy to miss.
The road gave us another clue.
Good attempt. Now let's make it safer.
This is why that rule exists.
streakLines: Three safe decisions in a row!
You are reading the road well.

chapters.title: Welcome to Roadsville
chapters.subtitle: Arrive, look around, feel the road

scenes.buddy: Welcome to Roadsville!
scenes.body: Lots of people. Lots of vehicles. Lots of places to go.

scenes.buddy: Imagine if everyone simply did whatever they wanted.
scenes.body: The road would become a very noisy puzzle! Luckily, roads have a system.

scenes.buddy: Tap what you notice. Small things matter on a busy street.

hotspots.label: Bus at the stop
hotspots.reveal: People are boarding and alighting. Give them space and time.

hotspots.label: Awkwardly parked scooter
hotspots.reveal: A parked vehicle can block sightlines for everyone else.

hotspots.label: Pedestrian waiting
hotspots.reveal: Someone is waiting to cross. Your next move affects them.

hotspots.label: Changing signal
hotspots.reveal: Signals create shared timing so traffic is predictable.

scenes.buddy: A vehicle ahead tries an unsafe cut. What should we do?
choices: Speed up and squeeze through
Slow down, create space, stay predictable
Honk continuously until they move

feedback.correct: Good road sense. Predictability keeps everyone safer.
feedback.incorrect: Rushing or aggression makes the puzzle worse. Slow and steady wins here.

chapters.title: The Road Basics
chapters.subtitle: A road is not an empty strip

scenes.buddy: A road is not just a big empty strip.
scenes.body: Edges, lanes, centre lines, and crossings all carry meaning. Let's touch each part.

scenes.buddy: Tap each part of the road to see why it exists.

hotspots.label: Road edge
hotspots.reveal: Edges mark where the carriageway ends. Stay within the usable road.

hotspots.label: Lane
hotspots.reveal: Lanes organise flow. Sudden wandering forces others to guess.

hotspots.label: Centre line
hotspots.reveal: Centre markings separate opposing or adjacent streams of traffic.

hotspots.label: Pedestrian area
hotspots.reveal: Crossings remind us the road is shared with people on foot.

scenes.buddy: This vehicle is drifting. Help it settle into the correct lane.
choices: Stay drifting — others will adapt
Check, indicate if needed, and settle into the correct lane
Cut across quickly without looking

feedback.correct: Much better. Other road users should not have to guess what you are about to do.
feedback.incorrect: Wandering or sudden cuts create confusion. Make your intention clear and calm.

chapters.title: Sign Forest
chapters.subtitle: Roads cannot talk — so they use signs

scenes.buddy: Roads cannot talk.
scenes.body: So they use signs. First we learn what they mean by looking — not by memorising a list.

scenes.buddy: This one is very clear.
scenes.prompt: You reach a Stop sign. What should you do?
choices: Slow a little and roll through if it looks clear
Stop fully, look carefully, then proceed when safe
Honk and continue because you are in a hurry

feedback.correct: Stop means stop. Look carefully before continuing.
feedback.incorrect: Rolling through skips the whole point of the sign. Give yourself time to see.

scenes.buddy: A warning sign says: pay attention.
scenes.prompt: You see a warning sign ahead. Best response?
choices: Ignore it until something happens
Prepare — slow down or heighten attention as needed
Speed up to get past the hazard faster

feedback.correct: Warnings buy you time. Use that time.
feedback.incorrect: Warnings exist because the road ahead may surprise you.

scenes.buddy: Match the situation to the right kind of sign.
scenes.prompt: Which sign family fits: movement not allowed here?
choices: Information sign
Prohibitory / mandatory restriction
Facility sign

feedback.correct: Sometimes the road is not asking. It is telling.
feedback.incorrect: When a movement is not allowed, look for prohibitory or mandatory guidance.

scenes.buddy: Junctions are where observation becomes really important.
scenes.body: Cross traffic, turns, pedestrians, signals — look wider than the car in front of you.

scenes.buddy: A pedestrian is still crossing.
choices: Continue immediately
Wait until it is safe
Repeatedly honk

feedback.correct: Good choice. The road is shared. Give people time and space.
feedback.incorrect: Being bigger does not mean you are always more important.

scenes.buddy: The signal says you may move. But can you actually clear the junction?
scenes.prompt: The light permits movement, yet traffic ahead is packed solid.
choices: Enter anyway — the signal said go
Wait until you can clear the junction without blocking it
Nose in and hope others make space

feedback.correct: Permission to move does not always mean it is safe or appropriate to enter.
feedback.incorrect: Blocking a junction traps everyone — including you.

scenes.buddy: Scan the junction. What is the biggest risk right now?
choices: A child near the kerb looking toward the road
A shop sign across the street
A parked car two streets away

feedback.correct: You spotted the risk early. Vulnerable users need extra care.
feedback.incorrect: Look for people who may step into the road with little warning.

scenes.buddy: Ready for a short challenge? I will talk less. You decide more.
scenes.body: Use what you learned in Roadsville so far — observe, think, decide safely.

scenes.buddy: Before asking ‘Can I pass?’ ask ‘Can I pass safely?’
scenes.prompt: Oncoming traffic is close and the road curves ahead.
choices: Overtake now to save time
Wait and observe — do nothing yet
Flash lights and force a gap

feedback.correct: Patience should be rewarded. Doing nothing yet can be the safest move.
feedback.incorrect: Overtaking is not a race. Visibility and space come first.

scenes.buddy: One more. Night is falling and a cyclist is hard to see.
choices: Keep normal day speed
Reduce speed, increase observation, give space
Pass as close as possible to finish quickly

feedback.correct: At night you may also have less time to react. Well judged.
feedback.incorrect: Lower visibility means more caution — not the same pace as daytime.

scenes.buddy: Do you remember your first minute in Roadsville?
scenes.body: The roads have not changed very much. But you have started to. Keep learning. Keep observing. Keep everyone safer.

scenes.buddy: People share this street. In Roadsville 3D, tap what you notice.
scenes.body: Walkers, children, and scooters move differently from cars. District: People on the Road.

scenes.buddy: A rider without a helmet is more vulnerable.
scenes.body: Slow down and leave space. District: No-Helmet Rider.

scenes.buddy: Near schools, expect sudden steps into the road.
scenes.body: District: School Zone — slow and watch the kerb.

scenes.buddy: Zebra means their turn.
scenes.body: Stop and let people finish crossing. District: Zebra Crossing.

chapters.title: Safe Ride Station
chapters.subtitle: Helmets, belts, lights, and starting ready
objectives: Wear your helmet before you start
Broken lights keep you off the road

scenes.buddy: Belts only protect if they are on before the surprise.
Helmet before kickstand up.
If they cannot see you, you do not belong on the road yet.
The road needs your full attention.

chapters.title: Lane and Movement
chapters.subtitle: Predictable moves — hills, beams, fog, priority

scenes.buddy: At many uncontrolled junctions, give way to traffic from the right.
On narrow hills, the climbing vehicle usually keeps the way.
Dip beams so the other driver can still see.
Fog needs low beam, lower speed, and honest gaps.
Before asking can I pass — ask can I pass safely.

chapters.title: Parking Puzzle
chapters.subtitle: Stopping is easy — stopping in the right place is clever

scenes.buddy: Where you stop can hide people and signs.
scenes.body: District: Parking Puzzle — use the marked bay.

scenes.buddy: No-parking signs protect sightlines and emergency access.
Align, reverse slowly, and finish inside the lines.
For injuries after a crash, call 108 or 102. When unsure, dial 112.

chapters.title: Real-World Roads
chapters.subtitle: Crashes, potholes, hospitals, wrong-way riders
objectives: Help without becoming the next crash

scenes.buddy: Protect the scene, then help.
Two-wheelers need room. Treat them as vulnerable road users.
Slow early. Only move aside when the path is truly clear.
Speed breakers work when you slow early and smoothly.
Near hospitals, quiet and calm keep the road humane.
Do not inherit a wrong-way risk.
Wet roads need earlier, gentler control.
At night you may also have less time to react.
Clear a safe path without creating new hazards.
Trains win every race. Waiting is the only win.
A patient gap keeps everyone predictable.

chapters.subtitle: Final destination
chapters.teaser: Return to Roadsville with new eyes — and earn ROAD READY.
